newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Moldova plans $70 mln Eurobond in April.
newsitem.headline: Moldova plans $70 mln Eurobond in April.

text.p: Moldova plans to place its first $70 million issue of Eurobonds on international markets in April, Finance Minister Valeriu Chitan said on Monday.
Chitan told a news conference that Merrill Lynch International would act as the Moldovan government's agent on the Eurobond placement.
Merrill Lynch helped Moldova make a $30 million international private placement last year, the first time the former Soviet republic had tapped international markets.
The private placement matures in December 1999, but is callable after two years. Denominations are $10,000 and $50,000, and annual interest will total around 11 percent.

Moldova initially planned to issue up to $50 million-worth of Eurobonds with a three-year maturity. But Moody's assigned it a Ba2 sovereign ceiling rating in January and the government and Merrill Lynch agreed to issue a bond of at least five years for $70 million.
Chitan said Moldova planned to borrow at 7-10 percent per annum, but final conditions would be fixed in April.

The bulk of the issue would be placed in Europe, but 10-15 percent would be sold in the United States. The cash from the issue would be used to service existing foreign debts and to repay pension and salary arrears.
Chitan said talks in London with 35 investors showed that Western banks, pension funds and insurance companies were interested not only in Moldovan Eurobonds, but also in domestic T-bills.
"We are ready to help foreign investors participate in Moldova's state securities market through local commercial banks," Chitan said.
"Competition from foreign investors will allow us to lower the price of internal T-bills and to channel financial resources to invest in production."
He said the government expected domestic interest rates to fall after the Eurobond issue. The National Bank discount rate is 20 percent while refinancing rates average 35-40 percent.

Chitan said Merrill Lynch would also help Moldova to issue $140 million of state promissory notes to be passed to Russian gas monopoly Gazprom as part of a deal on restructuring Moldova's $400 million debt to the gas monopoly.
